subject.title: WebChat: a config-change gateway restart drops the in-flight turn (empty/failed session, recovery can't resume, no user notice)

question: Should the first accepted fix for this issue be the scoped persistent WebChat recovery notice, or should maintainers require restart deferral or immediate user-message persistence before closing the issue?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the issue names three possible remedies with different user-state and persisted-transcript contracts; automation should not pick that product boundary while an open candidate PR already exists.

options.title: Accept Scoped Notice Fix
options.body: Land or rework the linked PR so WebChat users see a durable interrupted-turn notice, then track restart deferral and request preservation separately.

options.title: Require Full Request Preservation
options.body: Hold the linked PR until the implementation also persists the inbound user message or resumes the interrupted request rather than only surfacing a resend notice.

options.title: Redesign Restart Deferral First
options.body: Defer the notice-only fix until the gateway restart policy reliably waits for active WebChat turns or exposes a deliberate timeout contract.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Notice Fix
recommendation.body: Land or rework the linked PR so WebChat users see a durable interrupted-turn notice, then track restart deferral and request preservation separately.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows adjacent recovery storage and restart ownership work, and the remaining choice is a product/architecture boundary rather than a narrow code repair.
